records.name: Friends of the Wissahickon
records.summary: Volunteers who look after the trails, streams and woods of Wissahickon Valley Park. They hold public service days to clear drains, fix trails, pull invasive plants and pick up litter.
records.what_you_do: Join a registered service day to work on trails, plant, pull invasive vines and pick up trash. Trained volunteer corps take on longer roles such as trail ambassadors and crew leaders.

schedule.text: Public service days are posted on the group's upcoming dates page. A Thursday service day is listed for Oct 8, 2026 and a Saturday planting for Oct 10, 2026. Registration is required.

cost.text: No cost to volunteer is mentioned on the group's volunteer page.

first_step.how: Register for a listed service day on the group's volunteer sign-up page. Wear long pants and sturdy shoes, and bring sun protection and a water bottle.
first_step.basis: The group calls its service days the best place to start and says people without experience can join.

records.notes: Teens 14 to 18 may volunteer with a parent's signature on the waiver. Children under 14 must have an adult with them. Trail Ambassadors need an application and winter training (not checked). Wissahickon Trails (Montgomery County) co-presents a 2026 photo contest with this group and appears to be a separate organization.

records.name: BATONA Hiking Club
records.summary: A long-running hiking club that leads weekend hikes of about 5 to 15 miles at parks and trails around the region. Members also help maintain sections of the Batona, Horseshoe and Appalachian Trails.
records.what_you_do: Join a hike with a listed leader and check its length and difficulty before you go. Members can also join trail maintenance days, the annual dinner and a yearly hike and picnic.

schedule.text: Hikes most weekends, each with its own date, meeting time, length and difficulty on the club's site. Listed hikes run from October through mid-November 2026.

locations.label: Hikes at parks and trails in Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Delaware and Maryland

cost.text: Hikes list a $1 cost. The annual dinner is $25 a person.

first_step.how: Pick a hike on the club's site and RSVP through Meetup or the hike leader, as each listing says. Membership has an application form on the site.
first_step.basis: Hikes are listed publicly with leaders and difficulty, but the site does not plainly say whether non-members can join.

records.notes: Founding year is not stated on the site. Anniversary dinners in 2014 and 2015 suggest about 1928, which is our inference, not recorded. Dues are not published on the club's site, so none are recorded. The annual dinner organizer's personal contact is left out on purpose.

records.name: Latino Outdoors Philadelphia
records.summary: The Philadelphia chapter of Latino Outdoors, a national group that helps Latino communities enjoy nature. The chapter plans bike rides, kayaking, camping, climbing nights, river yoga and park restoration days.
records.what_you_do: Join a planned outing or volunteer day such as a trail ride, a kayak trip, a camping weekend, a bouldering night or a restoration day. Each event has its own sign-up page.

schedule.text: Outings and events, often monthly, from bike rides and kayaking to camping weekends, climbing nights and volunteer days. Upcoming events are posted with their own sign-up pages.

locations.label: Philadelphia-area trails, rivers and parks (the site is different for each outing)

cost.text: Varies by event. Check each event's sign-up page.

first_step.how: Pick an upcoming event on the group's link page and sign up through its event page. Some events need pre-registration.
first_step.basis: Events are open to the public and have sign-up pages, but no beginner program is described.

records.notes: The group's link page lists 2026 outings from February to September, including a Sept 12 to 13 camping weekend. Its 'Upcoming Events' section says 'In Planning', so confirm future dates before promising any. The national site's volunteer list shows a Philadelphia location filter but no chapter page. No website or email was shown for the chapter in text we could read.

records.name: Black Girls Hike Philly
records.summary: A community group that helps Black women get outside for their health and peace of mind, with guided hikes, trail runs, wellness retreats and learning walks.
records.what_you_do: Join a guided hike, trail run or meetup, or a wellness retreat. The group says it hopes to start youth programs and work with local parks.

schedule.text: Hikes and meetups are announced on the group's social media. No published calendar was found in the sources checked.

cost.text: Not stated in the sources checked.

first_step.how: Follow the group's public Instagram page for the next hike or meetup, and contact the group there.
first_step.basis: Open to Black women through public social pages, but no beginner program is described.

records.notes: No website. The web address listed on the funder's page is not a valid link, so the Instagram page is the only contact. The only dated item is a grant listing from November 2025, so the 'active' status rests on that. Verify before trusting it. The City Cast list (undated) says the group has been active for over three years, which is not used as a date.

records.name: Hike + Heal
records.summary: A women's hiking and wellness group that runs healing hikes, weekday happy hour hikes, field trips and retreats for women of all fitness levels.
records.what_you_do: Join a healing hike or happy hour hike, a wellness event, a field trip or a retreat. Events are posted on its calendar, and some are hosted with partner groups.

schedule.text: Healing hikes, weekday happy hour hikes, wellness events and retreats, listed on the group's calendar. The website shows no dates.

locations.label: Events in the Philadelphia suburbs and Wilmington, DE, per its calendar

cost.text: Price not shown on the website. Check each event listing.

first_step.how: Sign up for an event on the group's calendar, or use the 'join our next hike' button on the website.
first_step.basis: The site says women of all fitness levels are welcome, that no experience is needed, and it has a clear sign-up path for the next hike.

records.notes: Working site with no dated events. Its copyright line says 2024, which is not counted as evidence. Its calendar events are undated, including a Wilmington hayride and a Blue Bell photo hike co-hosted with Friends of the Wissahickon. Membership price is not shown on the site, so a price from an undated list article is not used. Check whether it serves Philadelphia residents before relying on in_city.

records.name: Discovery Pathways
records.summary: A South Philadelphia nonprofit that helps youth and families get outdoors. It runs free boating and family fishing days at FDR Park, a youth dragon boat team, environmental leadership classes, and park and waterway greening work.
records.what_you_do: Come to free boating on a Saturday or family fishing on a Wednesday at FDR Park. Youth can join the dragon boat team, the leadership program or greening work through the website.

schedule.text: Free Community Boating Days on Saturdays, 10 am to 1:30 pm, March 21 to Oct 17, 2026. Free Family Fishing on Wednesdays, 4 to 6:30 pm, April 22 to Aug 5 and Sept 16 to Oct 28, 2026. Youth programs run on their own schedules.

first_step.how: Show up on a Saturday for boating or a Wednesday for fishing at FDR Park. No sign-up is needed for those days. Youth programs use the youth application on the website.
first_step.basis: Boating days need no experience, no sign-up and include boats and instruction. Children must come with a guardian.

records.notes: Fishing is not one of our tags, so it appears in the summary only. Life jacket provision is not stated on the boating page. Dragon boat details are on a program page we did not read. The homepage's only dated item is a 2025 award. Active status rests on the 2026 season dates on the boating page.

records.name: Delaware Valley Orienteering Association
records.summary: A club that runs about 45 public orienteering events a year, where people use a map and compass to find checkpoints in parks. Beginners always get instruction at events.
records.what_you_do: Walk or jog a course with a map and compass, punching checkpoints along the way. Beginners get instruction and can take part without experience.

schedule.text: About 45 events a year at parks and environmental centers, typically 10 am to 1 pm, with registration until 1 pm. Dates are on the club's event schedule.

locations.label: Parks and environmental centers in eastern PA, northern DE, northern MD, and central and southern NJ

cost.text: Members pay reduced event fees. Map and event prices are on the club's pricing sheet.

first_step.how: Pick an event from the club's schedule and come on the day, or join online at dvoa.org/join.
first_step.basis: The club says events are open to the public and beginners always get instruction.

records.notes: The club's site names no Philadelphia venue (Nolde appears only in a photo caption), so in_city is false. Confirm whether any event runs in Philadelphia parks before relying on it. The 2026 schedule PDF could not be read by our fetch tool (compressed text), so no event dates are recorded from it. The mailing address is not recorded. Orienteering is not one of our tags, so 'hiking' is the closest fit.

records.name: Wyncote Audubon Society
records.summary: A local chapter of the Audubon bird network that has led free bird walks in Montgomery County parks and co-hosted walks at Pennypack Park. The most recent walk series we found ended in June 2024.
records.what_you_do: Walk with experienced birders to spot and identify local and migrating birds. Past walks were open to beginners.

schedule.text: Early-morning walks at High School Park were held on the third Saturday of each month, usually 7 to 8:30 am, through June 2024. No current walk calendar was found.

locations.label: High School Park, Elkins Park
locations.address: Montgomery Ave and High School Rd

cost.text: The High School Park page does not say whether walks are free. Some partner listings say free or by donation.

first_step.how: No current contact or calendar was found. Check the Friends of High School Park site for walk dates.
first_step.basis: Past walks were announced as open to beginners and experienced birders. No current newcomer program was found.

records.notes: No Wyncote website was found. Our searches found walks from 2018 to 2024 only. The name may have changed, since one directory lists Liberty Bird Alliance as formerly Wyncote Audubon. A Wissahickon Trails bird walk names Wyncote as co-host, but its year is not shown (Sunday, April 30), so it is not used. Dormant status keeps it in browse with a label.

records.name: Bartram's Garden
records.summary: A nearly 50 acre public garden and farm on the Schuylkill River in Southwest Philadelphia. Volunteers help at its Sankofa Community Farm, and a Thursday walking group meets there.
records.what_you_do: Help on Sankofa Community Farm volunteer days, join the Thursday walking group, or come to the garden's river and boathouse programs and events.

schedule.text: Sankofa Community Farm volunteer day on Saturday, Oct 10, 2026 at 9:30 am. WeWalk PHL Thursday walking group at 5 pm. Welcome Center open Thursday to Monday, 9:30 am to 4:30 pm.

cost.text: No admission or program fees are stated on the home page.

first_step.how: Come to the Thursday walking group at 5 pm, or check the website for the next Sankofa farm volunteer day.
first_step.basis: Walks and volunteer days are listed publicly with times, but no newcomer program is described.

records.notes: The Dock and Community Boathouse gives access to the Tidal Schuylkill, but the home page lists no boating hours or fees. A 2015 blog post describes free Saturday kayak and rowboat rides, and older pages describe free weekly fishing. Neither is confirmed for 2026, so neither is stated. The Sept 28, 2026 blog post on the leadership team is the newest dated item.

records.name: Outdoor Club of South Jersey
records.notes: Based in Oceanville, NJ. Its site names no Philadelphia outings and its meetings are in South Jersey. Surfaced through the Inquirer's June 2025 club list. Not recorded for this directory.

records.name: Wissahickon Trails
records.notes: Formerly the Wissahickon Valley Watershed Association, based in Ambler in Montgomery County. Its mission and listed events are in Montgomery County, so it is out of area for this directory. It co-presents a 2026 photo contest with Friends of the Wissahickon and co-hosts bird walks with Wyncote Audubon.

leads_only.name: Philly Trail Wanderers
leads_only.note: Hiking group on Meetup, named in a search roundup. Leads only, not checked.

leads_only.name: Philadelphia Hiking and Adventure Group
leads_only.note: Free Meetup hiking group named in an older Philadelphia Magazine article. Leads only, not checked. The article looks several years old.

leads_only.name: Body Liberation Hiking Club, Greater Philly chapter
leads_only.note: Chapter Instagram. The national site (bodyliberationoutdoorclub.org) was read and names no Philadelphia chapter page. Needs a dated post or a chapter page to confirm.

leads_only.name: OUT on the Trails
leads_only.note: Queer outdoor subgroup of Sip City Mixer, with free seasonal hikes, climbing and birding per a City Cast list. No website or dated post found. Needs one to confirm.

blocked.note: Home page returns 403 to our fetcher, and so does https://dvoc.org/events/cw_9_6_25/. Delaware Valley Ornithological Club and its BirdPHILLY walks are NOT recorded. Retry next run. Do not work around the 403.

notes: Second sweep of outdoors-adventure. Searches: 10 of 10 used, so the hard cap is reached. Fetches: about 27, including redirects and retries. Groups already on our list were skipped. GAPS: (1) Delaware Valley Ornithological Club (DVOC) and its BirdPHILLY walks are the biggest miss, because dvoc.org returned 403; search snippets showed walks from August to September 2026, which we could not read, so they are not recorded. (2) No backpacking or camping club was found, and no search budget was left for it. (3) No Philadelphia geocaching group was found. Stockton Geocaching Club is in Galloway, NJ, so it is out of area. GeoPhilly is a 2013-era mapping group, not outdoors. (4) Sierra Club Philadelphia Outdoors for All returned empty page content on two tries (not a 403). Not recorded; retry next run. (5) Brown Girls Climb and Outdoor Afro: no Philadelphia chapter was found in search results. Brown Girls Climb chapters shown are in DC, MD and VA. Outdoor Afro's own site was not checked. (6) No Philadelphia youth fishing club was found. Free family fishing at FDR Park is recorded under Discovery Pathways (2026 dates). Fish Hatchery at Pleasant Hill Park and Learn to Fish at Lardner's Point were seen only on 2024 pages, not checked. DROPPED WITH REASON: Bicycle Coalition of Greater Philadelphia (cycling lane, not in my family); Black Girl Joy Bike Ride and Black Girls Run Philadelphia (running and cycling lanes, no verified URLs); Vesper Boat Club, Fairmount Rowing Association, Schuylkill Navy and Wissinoming Yacht Club (water-rowing lane; the only URLs were from an AI-generated directory, so not used); Schuylkill River Development Corporation (no verified URL); Hidden River Outfitters (paid guided tours, a business with no community program); Philadelphia Rock Gyms outings (a business program with an undated price); In Color Birding Club (seen in a list summary, no URL found); Sip City Mixer (parent of OUT on the Trails, social lane, no site URL found); Discovery Pathways' partners. Personal contacts (a dinner organizer at BATONA, a secretary's details at DVOA) are not recorded beyond the club's published general email. Confidence and newcomer ratings are judgments from the group's own wording. Records with in_city false (DVOA, Wyncote, Hike + Heal, BATONA) need a human check of whether they serve Philadelphia residents. Suggested next steps: retry dvoc.org and the Sierra Club page, search for a backpacking club and In Color Birding Club, and check whether Black Girls Hike Philly has a current site.
